Create a complete single self-contained file `chip8_openrouter-google-gemini-3.8-flash_01.html` (HTML + CSS + JavaScript inline;
no external libraries, CDNs, assets or backend). Build a working CHIP-8 emulator.

Implement the interpreter properly: 4 KB of memory with the font set loaded at 0x050 and programs at 0x200,
sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF, the 16-bit index register, the program counter, a call stack, and the
delay and sound timers counting down at 60 Hz. Decode and execute the complete instruction set of 35
instructions, including the arithmetic and logic group with the carry and borrow flags in VF, the shift
instructions, jumps and calls, the random instruction, BCD conversion, register save and load, and the key
tests.

The display is 64 by 32 pixels drawn on a canvas scaled to a readable size, with sprites drawn by XOR and
the collision flag set in VF. The 16-key keypad is mapped to a 4 by 4 block of keyboard keys shown in the
interface; key press and release must both reach the emulator.

Include a small demo ROM as a byte array inside the file: a real program, assembled by you, that draws a
sprite and moves or reacts to a key, so that the emulator can be tried without any download. Also allow
loading a ROM from a local file.

Add run, pause, single step and reset controls, an adjustable instructions-per-frame speed, and a debugger
panel showing the registers, the index register, the program counter, the stack and the decoded current
instruction. Every visible control must work. Deliver the one file `chip8_openrouter-google-gemini-3.8-flash_01.html`.

- CHIP-8 CPU / Memory / Interpreter implementation:

  - Program loading starting at 0x200
  - Sixteen 8-bit registers V0 to VF
  - 16-bit index register I
  - 16-bit Program Counter PC initialized to 0x200
  - 16-level call stack and stack pointer SP
  - Delay timer and Sound timer counting down at 60 Hz (with Web Audio API synthesized beep when ST > 0)
  - Display buffer 64x32 monochrome, drawn to HTML5 canvas with upscale rendering and retro phosphor / glow / customizable colors or nice cyber/retro aesthetic.
  - Complete 35 CHIP-8 opcodes accurately implemented:
    * 00E0: CLS (clear screen)
    * 00EE: RET (return from subroutine)
    * 0NNN: SYS addr (ignored/treated as NOP or jump)
    * 1NNN: JP addr
    * 2NNN: CALL addr
    * 3XNN: SE Vx, byte (skip if Vx == byte)
    * 4XNN: SNE Vx, byte (skip if Vx != byte)
    * 5XY0: SE Vx, Vy (skip if Vx == Vy)
    * 6XNN: LD Vx, byte (Vx = byte)
    * 7XNN: ADD Vx, byte (Vx = (Vx + byte) & 0xFF, no flag change)
    * 8XY0: LD Vx, Vy
    * 8XY1: OR Vx, Vy (Vx = Vx | Vy, flag logic clean)
    * 8XY2: AND Vx, Vy (Vx = Vx & Vy)
    * 8XY3: XOR Vx, Vy (Vx = Vx ^ Vy)
    * 8XY4: ADD Vx, Vy (Vx = (Vx + Vy) & 0xFF, VF = carry: 1 if sum > 255 else 0)
    * 8XY5: SUB Vx, Vy (Vx = (Vx - Vy) & 0xFF, VF = NOT borrow: 1 if Vx >= Vy else 0)
    * 8XY6: SHR Vx {, Vy} (configurable / standard COSMAC VIP behavior with Vy or modern Vx >> 1; set VF to LSB of Vx before shift, Vx = (Vx >> 1) & 0xFF)
    * 8XY7: SUBN Vx, Vy (Vx = (Vy - Vx) & 0xFF, VF = NOT borrow: 1 if Vy >= Vx else 0)
    * 8XYE: SHL Vx {, Vy} (set VF to MSB (Vx >> 7) & 1, Vx = (Vx << 1) & 0xFF)
    * 9XY0: SNE Vx, Vy (skip if Vx != Vy)
    * ANNN: LD I, addr (I = NNN)
    * BNNN: JP V0, addr (PC = NNN + V0)
    * CXNN: RND Vx, byte (Vx = Math.floor(Math.random() * 256) & byte)

    * EXA1: SKNP Vx (skip next instruction if key in Vx is NOT pressed)
    * FX07: LD Vx, DT (Vx = delay timer)
    * FX0A: LD Vx, K (wait for key press, store key in Vx - execution halts until key pressed and released)
    * FX15: LD DT, Vx (delay timer = Vx)
    * FX18: LD ST, Vx (sound timer = Vx)
    * FX1E: LD I, Vx (I = (I + Vx) & 0xFFFF)
    * FX29: LD F, Vx (I = address of 5-byte font sprite for digit in Vx: 0x050 + (Vx & 0xF) * 5)
    * FX33: LD B, Vx (store BCD representation of Vx in memory at I, I+1, I+2: hundreds, tens, ones)
    * FX55: LD [I], Vx (store V0 through Vx inclusive into memory starting at address I; standard modern or VIP toggle, increments or keeps I)
    * FX65: LD Vx, [I] (read V0 through Vx inclusive from memory starting at address I)

    Keypad layout:
    1 2 3 C   ->  1 2 3 4
    4 5 6 D   ->  Q W E R
    7 8 9 E   ->  A S D F
    A 0 B F   ->  Z X C V
    Show on-screen interactive keypad with visual feedback when pressed (can click on-screen buttons or use keyboard).
  - Built-in interactive demo ROMs:
    1) "Sprite Wanderer & Keypad Test" - Assembled demo ROM byte array: Draws an animated/moving spaceship/player sprite, displays coordinates or responds to directional keys (W/A/S/D or 2/4/6/8/5) with bouncing and sound beep, testing drawing, collision, keys, timer, and arithmetic!
    2) "Keypad Tester / Sound Test" - Simple interactive key inspection demo.
    Also file input to load custom .ch8 ROM files via drag-and-drop or file picker button.
  - Controls:
    * Run / Pause toggle button
    * Single Step button
    * Reset button
    * Speed slider (instructions per frame: 1 to 50, default ~10-15; runs smoothly at 60Hz requestAnimationFrame)
    * Beep sound mute toggle
    * Theme / Color palette selector (Green phosphor, Amber, Cyberpunk Neon, Classic White/Black, Game Boy)
  - Debugger panel:
    * Registers V0 to VF (hex and dec display, highlighting changed values)
    * Index Register (I), Program Counter (PC), Stack Pointer (SP)
    * Delay Timer (DT) and Sound Timer (ST)
    * Current instruction disassembled / decoded into readable mnemonic (e.g. "D015 - DRW V0, V1, 5")
    * Disassembly view of upcoming instructions around PC
    * Stack contents view
  - Sleek, polished retro-cyberpunk UI layout with clear typography, canvas display, debugger panel, keypad visualizer, control toolbar, and instruction guide. All in a single self-contained file with no external dependencies.","path":"chip8_openrouter-google-gemini-3.8-flash_01.html"}
